title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, complete execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostics, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants: required sequencing, policy compliance, loop- and dependency-safety, and group-level rollout constraints. Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility but leave open questions about how much deterministic verification and bounded automated repair change operational correctness when paired comparisons reuse the exact same sampled initial candidate. This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-grounded paired experiment that isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Research question and estimand. Preregistered study CAND-2026-001 asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not measure benefits from independent guarded first-pass re-generation, prompt constraints, or multi-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini). (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Reproducibility guidance and bounded limitations tied to archived artifacts and reconciliation records.
sections.related_work:
We performed a fresh literature investigation and verified records covering intent→configuration systems, generate–validate–repair patterns, and agentic-AI safety discussions relevant to NetOps. Prior intent-to-configuration prototypes and task-bench evaluations demonstrate that LLMs can synthesize device configurations from operator intents and that verification is widely recommended as a guardrail [1],[2],[3]. Work in adjacent domains (program repair, test-driven repair) documents that generate→validate→repair patterns can improve correctness, motivating guarded pipelines in operational settings [4],[5]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM deployment document failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and argue for verifier gates and provenance [6].

Synthesis and gap. The verified records show active work on intent-driven generators and proposals for guardrails, but they leave an empirical gap: few artifact-backed studies quantify the marginal verifier/repair effect when the exact same initial generated candidate is reused across conditions. Our paired shared_initial_candidate design directly addresses that gap and yields an artifact-grounded measurement of a repair-only effect under deterministic verification.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before execution (preregistration SHA-256 noted in the execution manifest). The preregistration specified: primary estimand, deterministic sampling plan selecting 200 tasks from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), at most one automated repair call per task, the confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar), primary failure handling, sensitivity analyses, and power rationale targeting detection of ≈10–15 percentage-point paired increases at N = 200 for baseline assumptions near 45–65%.

Task bank and encoding. Tasks were generated deterministically (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and targeted high-difficulty workflows (very_hard and extreme). Each task manifest encodes: initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered list of configuration commands that must appear in the correct order), allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., at-least-one-up constraints), difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count), and a normalized reference_answer. Representative archived tasks show required_command_count values from 3 up to 9 and changed_interface_count up to 3 for extreme tasks; these fields are stored in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and in representative task entries in the artifact bundle.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared requested model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). That record shows temperature = null (unset). Per preregistration and Methods we explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; the hosted model service may sample nondeterministically. The adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The provider-call audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, confirming the execution adhered to the preregistered call budget.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rule. A deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) served as the oracle. The verifier: parses candidate configurations, enforces per-device allowed-field constraints, checks required_sequence ordering constraints, evaluates group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up, final_group_constraints), and validates dependency rules encoded in the task manifest. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 iff all encoded invariants pass. Per-episode validator_trace artifacts include validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag. These traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ and are the primary evidence for per-episode scoring.

Paired execution semantics, failure handling, and contamination controls. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for each pair begin from the identical sampled candidate; any paired difference therefore arises solely from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The preregistered missingness_plan specified deterministic sanitizer attempts for minor formatting issues and a sensitivity analysis treating persistent unparsables as failures. The contamination plan included deterministic pre-use deduplication of vendor templates and token-similarity checks; analysis/contamination_summary.csv documents flagged contamination (empty in this run). Deterministic_reconciliation.json records cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0, indicating fresh generation events for all shared initial calls.

Statistical analysis and exact McNemar implementation. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar based on discordant pair counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). Let n = n10 + n01 and k = n10. Under H0 (no directionality) k ~ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p-value is computed exactly with the binomial tails: p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)}, with the standard treatment when k = 0. For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this calculation yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile confidence intervals for the absolute risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; these parameters and the bootstrap implementation are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started at 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed at 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (≈29 minutes wall-clock). Planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, matching the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the single permitted repair call.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. analysis/condition_summary.csv records:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Using the exact two-sided McNemar binomial calculation described in Methods (n = 1, k = 1) yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]; these values appear in analysis/results.json and the archived CSV artifacts.

Single repaired case: diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Validator traces for the repaired pair (archived under execution/scoring/ for the episode where the repair stage was consumed) show repair_applied = true in the verifier_trace and document a required_sequence ordering violation in validation_before.violation_codes; validation_after.valid = true after a minimal reordering repair. Manifest metadata classifies that task as extreme with required_command_count near the upper range (representative manifests show required_command_count up to 9 and changed_interface_count up to 3). The localized correction was an ordering adjustment that preserved allowed_touched_fields and satisfied group invariants; the archived validator_trace contains the pre-repair violation codes and the repaired normalized_configuration demonstrating the minimal change.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination. analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros in all missingness categories; there were no preregistered exclusions. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty; deterministic_reconciliation.json marks all deterministic consistency checks passed and pair_accounting_consistent = true. These artifacts confirm the run completed all preregistered episodes without persistent unparsables or contamination flags.

Exploratory diagnostics. Representative task manifests illustrate difficulty heterogeneity: required_command_count ranged 3–9 and difficulty tags included very_hard and extreme. The single baseline failure occurred in the extreme stratum, aligning with the preregistered exploratory expectation that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity increase failure risk. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (archived) visualizes the bootstrap distribution used for the CI and condition rates.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation and practical meaning. Because the experiment used shared_initial_candidate semantics, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on the identical sampled candidate. In other words, this is a repair-only effect: the guarded condition did not benefit from a different first-pass generation. This design avoids confounding from sampling variance or constrained-guarded prompting but explicitly does not measure the broader class of guarded interventions such as independent guarded first-pass generation, multi-sampling selection, or constrained prompts.

Statistical regime and power consequences. The preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 pp) at N = 200 assuming baseline rates near 45–65%. The actual baseline rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those assumptions, moving the analysis into a discrete discordant-count regime with only one discordant pair. In that regime the exact McNemar p-value is uninformative (p = 1.0) but the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] provides a practical bound on plausible effect sizes consistent with the data. The outcome demonstrates a common pragmatic lesson: prespecified power targets can be frustrated by unexpectedly high baseline performance and the resulting discrete inference regime.

Operational implications and bounded claims. Artifact-grounded evidence supports the narrow operational conclusion that verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct a localized ordering fault in an extreme composite synthetic task for gpt-5-mini under the chosen verifier. This single corrected case involved a sequencing dependency across multiple interfaces and required only a minimal reordering repair. We do not claim that verifier-guarded repair will systematically correct omissions visible only in dataplane execution, semantic intent misunderstandings, or adversarially induced fabrications. Broader operational claims require multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded designs, emulation or dataplane tests, and adversarial contamination experiments.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate paired design removes sampling confounds and isolates repair-only effects, but it does not address prompt sensitivity or sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling). Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces the invariants encoded in the manifest but cannot substitute for live dataplane behavior or vendor-specific firmware quirks. External validity: the study used a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank; generalization to other models, prompting strategies, vendor firmware, or production heterogeneity is not established. Conclusion validity: with only one discordant pair, statistical sensitivity to small absolute effects is limited; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and artifact guidance. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and indexed by the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Key artifacts for reanalysis: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (task selection and manifests), execution/model_configuration.json (declared model and sampling fields), execution/responses/ (shared-initial and per-condition responses), execution/scoring/ (validator_trace per episode), analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (confirmatory summaries), deterministic_reconciliation.json (provider accounting and stage_counts), and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap parameters and seed). Re-running the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor against execution/raw_results.jsonl reproduces the numbers reported above. The initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 included in the Disclosure Statement) and the model_configuration.json records temperature = null; per Methods, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the observed discordants. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest (paths: execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/responses/, execution/scoring/, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json).
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
